analysis: No verified fills yet — the strategy has proposed trades but none filled inside displayed depth and limits (see its intents), or its trigger conditions have not met on the captured universe.

evidence.claim: Mean reversion vs momentum in short-horizon binaries is an open question for event contracts; treated as a hypothesis to be tested on this data, not assumed.

failure_mode: If the move is news (a real regime change), the fade keeps losing: adverse selection is the whole story. The backtest on verified candles decides whether this rule even earns a forward slot.
name: 10c Mean Reversion
rule: When |last - previous| >= 0.10: if last <= previous - 0.10 and last <= 0.45, buy YES at its ask (limit ask + 2c); if last >= previous + 0.10 and last >= 0.55, buy NO at its ask. Size 15% of cash. Exit at 2x entry if the bid reaches it, else hold to settlement.
why: Large one-day moves on binary contracts can overshoot: paying <= 45c for a side that 'dropped' 10c is betting the move exaggerated. The 2x target caps the winner size; settlement is the default exit.
